_format: Evidence entries for the detail modal. by_topic: topic × party arrays. by_person: person id → results timeline. Sources: official 2024 GE manifestos + Hansard speeches. Every quote is verbatim.

lisa-nandy.headline: Nandy at LGA Conference: housing as social infrastructure
lisa-nandy.quote: Decent housing is a foundation, not a privilege — and a healthy nation knows the difference.

lisa-nandy.headline: Conference speech: rebuilding civic life
lisa-nandy.quote: Communities are not a sentimental idea — they are how a country actually functions.

robert-jenrick.headline: Jenrick: Renters' Rights Bill will 'shrink the rental market'
robert-jenrick.quote: Reform must work for renters and landlords. Tilting the field destroys both.

robert-jenrick.headline: Conference speech: a fairer settlement on housing
robert-jenrick.quote: We need to build, not regulate our way out of the housing crisis.

daisy-cooper.headline: Cooper: rent caps a 'short-term fix'
daisy-cooper.quote: Build more, regulate fairly, end no-fault evictions. That's the formula.

daisy-cooper.headline: Tabled amendment for national landlord register
daisy-cooper.quote: A national register of landlords is the floor, not the ceiling.

labour.headline: Labour: growth must benefit everyone, not just a few
labour.quote: Kickstart economic growth to secure the highest sustained growth in the G7, with good jobs and productivity growth in every part of the country making everyone, not just a few, better off.

conservative.headline: Conservatives: economy is turning a corner on strong foundations
conservative.quote: The economy is turning a corner because we built strong economic foundations before the pandemic and we have stuck to our plan.

libdem.headline: Lib Dems: build a strong, fair economy for everyone
libdem.quote: Liberal Democrats will build a strong, fair economy that benefits everyone in the UK.

snp.headline: SNP: Scotland's economy grows faster per head than UK
snp.quote: We've grown the economy faster, per head, than the UK.

plaid.headline: Plaid Cymru demands needs-based funding to replace Barnett Formula
plaid.quote: Plaid Cymru believes that Wales should be funded according to our needs, not the out-dated Barnett Formula which instead provides funding proportionate to spending on England's needs.

labour.headline: Labour: mission is to build an NHS fit for the future
labour.quote: Labour's mission is to build an NHS fit for the future.

conservative.headline: Conservatives pledge 92,000 nurses and inflation-busting NHS spend
conservative.quote: Increase NHS spending above inflation every year, recruiting 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors.

libdem.headline: Lib Dems pledge GP appointment within 7 days for everyone
libdem.quote: Give everyone the right to see a GP within seven days, or within 24 hours if they urgently need to, with 8,000 more GPs to deliver on it.

snp.headline: SNP: Scotland has the best-performing A&E units in the UK
snp.quote: We have the best performing core A&E units in the UK.

plaid.headline: Plaid Cymru: healthcare free at the point of delivery, oppose privatisation
plaid.quote: Plaid Cymru strongly believes in the principle of healthcare free at the point of delivery, funded through general taxation. We oppose the privatisation of services by stealth through out-sourcing.

labour.headline: Labour pledges 6,500 new expert teachers in key subjects
labour.quote: Labour will recruit an additional 6,500 new expert teachers.

labour.headline: Labour MP challenges Conservatives on tuition fee legacy
labour.quote: Given that plan 2 tuition fees were introduced by the Conservatives in 2012, that they froze the repayment thresholds in 2016 and that they abolished the maintenance grants, was that fair then?

conservative.headline: Conservatives claim children are best readers in the West
conservative.quote: We recruited record numbers of teachers to help our children become the best readers in the West.

conservative.headline: Conservative MP: Labour first introduced tuition fees
conservative.quote: I must be suffering from some sort of political amnesia, because I was absolutely convinced that it was a Labour Government that introduced tuition fees in the first place. Maybe the Minister will correct me.

conservative.headline: Conservative MP: Labour has now admitted student loans system is broken
conservative.quote: In January, the Chancellor was saying that the student loans system was 'fair and reasonable'. She now admits 'as of yesterday' that it is broken. In one sense, we have won this debate even before it started.

libdem.headline: Lib Dems pledge dedicated mental health professional in every school
libdem.quote: Putting a dedicated, qualified mental health professional in every school.

snp.headline: SNP pledges to defend free university tuition in Scotland
snp.quote: Defend free university tuition in Scotland. The SNP is the only party that will protect students and defend free education.

snp.headline: SNP MP: Scotland's students pay no tuition fees
snp.quote: most income tax payers in Scotland pay less tax. Over and above that, her constituents do not have to pay for their tuition fees.

plaid.headline: Plaid Cymru: no child should struggle with the cost of education
plaid.quote: No child or family should struggle with the cost of education. No child should be hungry at school. It is only because of Plaid Cymru that all primary school children in Wales receive free school meals.

labour.headline: Labour pledges 1.5 million new homes next parliament
labour.quote: Labour will get Britain building again, creating jobs across England, with 1.5 million new homes over the next parliament.

labour.headline: Starmer hails biggest renters' rights upgrade in a generation
labour.quote: I am very proud — this Government are very proud — of the biggest upgrade in workers' rights in a generation and the biggest upgrade in renters' rights in a generation and of doing the most any Government have ever done to reduce child poverty.

labour.headline: Starmer: upgrading renters' rights and building 1.5 million homes
labour.quote: We are going to build 1.5 million homes. We are upgrading the rights of renters, because we know how important it is for everyone to have a safe and secure roof over their head.

conservative.headline: Conservatives pledge 1.6 million new homes in England
conservative.quote: We will deliver 1.6 million homes in England in the next Parliament.

libdem.headline: Lib Dems pledge to ban no-fault evictions immediately
libdem.quote: Delivering a fair deal for renters by immediately banning no-fault evictions, making three-year tenancies the default, and creating a national register of licensed landlords.

snp.headline: SNP: built 40% more affordable homes per head than England
snp.quote: We've built 40% more affordable homes per head than in England.

plaid.headline: Plaid Cymru: right to a safe and affordable home, with rent controls
plaid.quote: Plaid Cymru believes that everybody has the right to a safe and affordable home in their community, and this should be the purpose of the housing system. We will introduce a Right to Adequate Housing which will underpin this.

labour.headline: Labour pledges swift, firm and fair asylum system
labour.quote: Labour will restore order to the asylum system so that it operates swiftly, firmly, and fairly; and the rules are properly enforced.

conservative.headline: Conservatives pledge legal migration cap to guarantee falling numbers
conservative.quote: Introduce a legal cap on migration to guarantee that numbers will fall every year, so public services are protected while bringing in the skills we need.

conservative.headline: Conservative MP credits ETA scheme as Conservative border reform
conservative.quote: The ETA scheme was introduced by the Conservative Government to secure and modernise Britain's borders.

libdem.headline: Lib Dems pledge to scrap Rwanda scheme and uphold Refugee Convention
libdem.quote: Scrap the Conservatives' Illegal Migration Act and their Rwanda scheme, uphold the Refugee Convention, and provide safe and legal routes to sanctuary for refugees.

snp.headline: SNP demands devolved bespoke migration system for Scotland
snp.quote: Devolve powers to create a bespoke migration system for Scotland.

plaid.headline: Plaid Cymru opposes Rwanda deportations and demands UK uphold Refugee Treaty
plaid.quote: Plaid Cymru strongly oppose the Conservative UK Government's proposals and attitudes towards asylum seekers and refugees, including deportation to Rwanda and the general hostile environment created. We believe that the UK should uphold the commitments made when it signed up to the Refugee Treaty in 1951.

labour.headline: Labour pledges clean energy superpower status by 2030
labour.quote: Make Britain a clean energy superpower to cut bills, create jobs and deliver security with cheaper, zero-carbon electricity by 2030, accelerating to net zero.

conservative.headline: Conservatives promise affordable transition to sustainable energy
conservative.quote: Delivering an affordable transition to domestic, sustainable energy.

conservative.headline: Conservative MP: decarbonise affordably without harming communities
conservative.quote: We believe in decarbonisation, but we need to do it in a way that people can afford and that does not trash our country in the process.

libdem.headline: Lib Dems commit to net zero by 2045
libdem.quote: Take the action needed now to achieve net zero by 2045.

libdem.headline: Lib Dem peer: cost of oil crisis exceeds cost of net zero
libdem.quote: The Climate Change Committee was clear last week that the cost of another oil price crisis would be greater than the cost of reaching net zero by 2050, so these Benches fully support the need to roll out renewables at a faster rate.

snp.headline: SNP calls for fair and managed transition to net zero
snp.quote: Deliver a fair and managed transition to net zero.

plaid.headline: Plaid Cymru commits to net zero in Wales by 2035 and reversing biodiversity decline by 2030
plaid.quote: Plaid Cymru recognises that the climate and nature emergencies are the biggest threat to mankind on a global scale, and reaffirms our commitment to reaching net-zero targets in Wales by 2035 and reversing biodiversity decline by 2030.
